scope: conditional company-scale refrigerant scenarios at fixed FY2026 cooling service, adoption sensitivity through2031

sources.title: Walmart FY2026 ESG Report
sources.boundary: annual corporate operational emissions; not lifecycle damage or financial loss

sources.title: DOE/Navigant Transcritical Carbon Dioxide Supermarket Refrigeration Systems, January 2015
sources.page: printed 19-20 (PDF24-25), Table V.2; printed1 for comparison design
sources.geography: Hannaford Turner Maine versus Bradford Vermont, US
sources.period: Table V.2 caption September2013-July2014; surrounding prose calls year-long, inconsistency preserved
sources.baseline: HFC407A direct-expansion store versus transcriticalCO2 store with nearly identical layout/refrigeration loads and similar climate/vintage
sources.boundary: measured leakage mass with GWP-converted direct operational emissions; total table includes electricity/propane but not equipment embodied lifecycle; no randomized causal study
sources.limitations: Table values rounded; use approximately99.95%, not spurious precision. Executive summary has inconsistent191lb leak statement; use explicit TableV.2 mass rows and sectionV.F. Direct factor not a whole-store reduction factor. Different heat reclaim/heating performance; climate not fully normalized.

sources.title: Refrigerating with carbon dioxide boosts performance
sources.boundary: commercial deployment evidence; no energy efficacy used in this scenario

observed_pressure.interpretation: climate-pressure inventory metric, not monetized harm or proof emissions are unnecessary

model.q_definition: Share of baseline onsite-refrigerant CO2e arising from systems eligible AND replaced by2031; not share of stores, gas mass or cooling load
model.r_definition: Transferred direct leakage CO2e efficacy; 1-0.1/191 from DOE paired-store data, about99.95%
model.net_formula: A_net = A_direct - delta_electricity_MWh * matched_grid_tCO2e_per_MWh / 1e6 - delta_other_fuels_tCO2e/1e6 - incremental_lifecycle_tCO2e/1e6
model.service_constraint: Same food volumes, temperatures, cooling service and duty; adjust gas charge/leakage for actual installed equipment. No credit for cooling less.
model.gas_mix_caveat: Walmart actual emitted gas mix/charge/GWP basis unknown. Transfer valid only if treated emissions have Hannaford-comparable high-GWP baseline and CO2 alternative; restate GWP consistently before audited calculation. General r=1-(new emitted kg/old emitted kg)*(new GWP/old GWP).
model.horizon: Annual run-rate after conversion by2031; no cumulative five-year sum without installation schedule

scenarios.name: CONDITIONAL: 25% of FY2026 onsite-refrigerant emissions eligible and converted by 2031; Hannaford-like direct effect
scenarios.feasibility_status: q is a sensitivity, not demonstrated feasible adoption; r transfer requires matching system characteristics and GWP accounting

scenarios.feasibility_status: q is a sensitivity, not demonstrated feasible adoption; r transfer requires matching system characteristics and GWP accounting

scenarios.feasibility_status: q is a sensitivity, not demonstrated feasible adoption; r transfer requires matching system characteristics and GWP accounting

elimination_ceiling.name: THEORETICAL ONLY: eliminate100% onsite refrigerant emissions at fixed service, no secondary penalty
elimination_ceiling.status: Arithmetic ceiling, not demonstrated feasible process or adoption estimate; even CO2 can leak

pitch: Walmart reports4.08million tonnesCO2e yearly from onsite refrigerants. A real supermarket comparison shows that availableCO2 cooling can nearly eliminate direct refrigerant climate impact. If systems responsible for half that Walmart source could be converted with comparable performance, the gross opportunity would be about2.04million tonnes per year—14.2% of operational emissions—before energy/lifecycle effects and beyond-baseline additionality are checked.
finance: Technical opportunity is not investor additionality or repayable cashflow. Deduct committed upgrades; underwrite actual avoided operating costs and signed payments. No damage valuation assumed to be revenue.

gas-specific baseline and consistent GWP version
site electricity/heating changes and lifecycle impacts
